transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hi. Thank you for seeing me. I, um... I guess I'm just here because I've been feeling a little overwhelmed lately. It's probably nothing major, I mean, I know everyone gets stressed, but... I just can't seem to shake this feeling that everything going wrong is somehow my fault. 

Like, at work, I keep thinking I'm just a terrible employee, and then at home, I feel like I'm failing there too. Sometimes I even think I deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds really silly and dramatic, doesn't it? I just... I want to be doing a good job, and I feel like I'm letting everyone down. Is it okay that I'm bringing this up?
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time lately?

Um... I'm not really sure. I don't think I've been feeling sad, exactly. I mean, I have a good job and a nice life, so I really have no reason to be sad, right? I'd hate to sound ungrateful or like I'm just complaining over nothing. 

I haven't really noticed an empty feeling, either, I don't think. I mostly just worry about messing things up and letting people down. Is that... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do lately?

Um... well, I guess I've been a little less active lately. I used to love planning brunches with my friends, or, you know, going into the spare room to paint. I even went hiking a lot and signed up for all these networking events for work. 

But lately... I don't know, I guess I just haven't been as into it? It's not that I don't like those things anymore, I just... when I do them now, they feel more like tasks I'm just pretending to care about, if that makes sense. I still try to do them so I don't let anyone down, but the spark is kind of missing. 

I'm sorry, I know I should be more appreciative of having hobbies and friends to do things with. Does that sound like what you were asking? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Have you lost any weight recently?

Um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I haven't been actively trying to lose weight or anything, and I know I should be taking better care of myself. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm neglecting my health on purpose. 

My appetite has just been kind of... all over the place, I suppose. I mostly just end up skipping real meals during the day because I'm so focused on trying to get my work done right. And then I'll realize later that my clothes are feeling a bit looser. I think I've mostly just been living on coffee, maybe some toast, or whatever is easiest to grab so I don't waste time. 

I know I really need to do better with cooking proper meals. Is that... does that answer your question? I hope it's okay that I haven't been keeping very good track of the exact numbers on the scale.
Do you feel like you're no longer able to experience pleasure from activities that you used to enjoy?

Um... I think I might have mentioned this just a second ago, but... yeah, I guess I really don't get the same feeling out of things anymore. I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering you right.

Like I said, I used to love planning those weekend brunches, or going into the spare room to paint, and even hiking and going to all those networking events for work. I really did enjoy them. But now... it's just really hard to find that feeling. When I do those things now, it feels more like I'm just going through the motions, like they're chores I'm just pretending to care about so I don't upset anyone or seem lazy. 

I know it sounds awful to say that about spending time with friends or doing nice things, and I really am trying to be better about it. I just don't feel that spark of happiness from them right now. Does that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm making sense.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... well, it's been a little while, I guess. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I've just been sitting around feeling sorry for myself this whole time, because I really have been trying to push through and keep up with everything. 

But I suppose... if I really think about it, this feeling—the sadness and just not caring about my hobbies as much—it's been going on for about two years and one month. Roughly. I'm sorry, I know that sounds like a really long time to let something go without fixing it, and I probably should have said something sooner. I just kept hoping I could snap out of it on my own, you know? 

Is that... is that the right kind of timeline you were looking for? I hope it doesn't make me seem like I haven't been trying to get better.
Do you often feel guilty about things that you've done or haven't done?

Um... yeah, I guess I do. I mean, I try really hard not to let it get to me, because I know I should just be grateful for what I have. I don't want to sound unappreciative or like I'm complaining too much. 

But honestly, that's kind of a big part of why I finally came in to see someone. I just... I can't stop feeling like every little thing that goes wrong is entirely my fault. Like, if a project gets delayed at work, or if a pipe leaks at my house, my brain just immediately goes to, "I'm a terrible employee," or "I'm a horrible homeowner." It feels like I just deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for because I'm not doing a good enough job keeping it all together. 

I know it probably sounds silly to get so worked up over things I can't always control. I really am trying to be more positive, I promise. Does that... make sense? I hope I'm not overreacting by feeling this way.
Do you often criticize yourself for things that might not even be your fault?

Oh, um... yes, definitely. I think that ties right into what I was just rambling about a second ago... I'm so sorry, I hope I'm not repeating myself too much or talking in circles! 

But yes, I am really hard on myself. Like I mentioned with the work delays or the house... even if I logically know I didn't personally cause a pipe to burst, I still criticize myself over it. My brain just twists it into being my fault, and I end up telling myself I'm a bad homeowner or a bad employee. It just makes me feel like I deserve to lose everything I've worked for, even when I know that's probably an irrational way to look at it. 

I know it's not a very productive way to think, and I promise I really am trying to be kinder to myself. Am I... am I giving you the right kind of examples? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Do you feel worthless or have a significantly lowered opinion of yourself compared to before you started feeling overwhelmed?

Um... well, yes, I suppose I do. I mean, I really don't want to come across like I just hate myself or that I'm completely giving up. I know I have a lot of good things going for me, and I try to focus on that. 

But... yeah, I think my opinion of myself has definitely dropped since this all started. It's like I was saying before... that feeling of worthlessness is honestly the main reason I finally made this appointment. I just can't shake this awful feeling that I'm just fundamentally failing at everything. Like I'm a terrible employee, and a terrible homeowner... and that because of that, I just don't deserve any of the things I've worked so hard for. It just feels like I'm not worth it anymore. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds so dramatic, and I really am trying to snap out of it and be more confident again. I hope I'm not sounding too negative... is that the kind of information you needed for that question?
How long have you been feeling worthless or having a lowered opinion of yourself?

Um... well, it's been a little while. I really don't want to sound like I've just been wallowing in it or anything, because I've honestly been trying my best to push through and keep up with my job and everything else. 

But... I guess the depression, and just... losing interest in things I normally like... it's been with me for about two years and one month now. Give or take a little? I know that sounds like a really long time to let things go before getting help, and I'm so sorry I didn't come in sooner. I just kept hoping I could fix it myself and be back to normal without bothering anyone. 

Is... is it okay that I waited that long? I hope I'm giving you the right timeline, I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Do you feel worthless all the time or are there moments when you feel better about yourself?

Um... well, I try so hard to look on the bright side, so I really don't want to say I feel completely worthless every single second. I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining or not trying! 

But... if I'm being completely honest, looking back... the low mood and just that loss of interest in everything, it's pretty much been there for almost the whole time since this all started. There are definitely these brief periods where the cloud lifts a little, and I can function a bit better, you know? Like I can get my work done and feel okay for a minute, and I always try really hard to hold onto those good days so I don't let anyone down. 

But they usually just don't last very long before it goes back to how it was. I'm sorry, I hope that's not too discouraging to hear. I promise I'm trying my absolute best to have more of those better moments. Does... does that answer your question alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Are there any days when you don't feel worthless at all?

Um... well, yes, there are definitely days where I don't feel *completely* worthless. I really try to focus on those days! I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself all the time. 

But... I guess, like I mentioned earlier... the main reason I finally made this appointment is because I just can't stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault. Even on the better days, it's like this heavy guilt is just sitting there in the back of my mind. It's just... I keep feeling like I'm a bad employee, and a bad homeowner, and that I deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for. 

I'm so sorry, I know I'm kind of repeating myself, and I really don't mean to sound like a broken record or like I'm not trying to get better. I just... I can't seem to turn off that feeling that I'm just inherently doing everything wrong. Is... is it helpful that I'm explaining it this way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture without sounding too dramatic.
Are there any periods of time, even if just a few days, where you don't feel worthless at all?

Um... yes, actually! I really want to make sure I'm giving you the whole picture, and it hasn't been completely bad the entire time. There was actually a stretch of, oh, maybe several weeks where that heavy feeling lifted a bit. I was getting through work a lot more normally, which I was really happy about because I hate falling behind or being a burden to my team. 

But... um... I don't know if I should even mention this next part. I really don't want to sound crazy or make you think worse of me. But even during those weeks when my mood was better and I didn't feel so worthless... I, um... I still heard that voice near the air vents. And I was still completely convinced that the mortgage company and my coworkers were monitoring me. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds really strange and I probably shouldn't have let it go on without saying anything. I just want to be totally honest with you so you have all the facts to do your job. Did... did I explain that okay? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for.
Are your feelings of worthlessness present every day?

Um... well, like I was saying, there was that one stretch where it wasn't every single day. I really want to emphasize that, because I don't want to seem like I'm not trying to stay positive! 

But... I guess for the most part, yeah, it's pretty much an everyday thing. That's actually the main reason I finally decided to come in. I just... I can't stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is entirely my fault. It's like this constant loop in my head telling me I'm a terrible employee and a bad homeowner, and that I just deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for. 

I'm so sorry, I know I'm basically saying the same thing again. I really don't want to frustrate you or sound like I'm just whining. It's just so hard to shake that feeling, even when I'm trying my absolute best. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way.
Are there any periods of time, even if brief, where you feel completely worthy of the good things in your life?

Um... well, yes, like I mentioned just a bit ago, there was that one period. I really do try to hold onto those times to remind myself that things aren't always so dark. For a few weeks, my mood wasn't nearly as heavy, and I was actually getting through my work day pretty normally, which was such a relief because I hate feeling like I'm letting my team down.

But... um, I guess I should reiterate... even when I was feeling a bit more worthy and capable during those weeks, the other stuff didn't stop. I still... I still heard that voice by the air vents. And I was still just as certain that the mortgage company and the people at work were keeping tabs on me. 

I'm so sorry to keep bringing that up, I know it probably sounds so bizarre and I really don't want you to think I'm completely losing my mind. I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details. Is... is it okay that I'm explaining it this way? I just want to be a good patient and give you what you need.
Are there any times when you feel completely worthy of the good things in your life without any doubts or guilt?

Um... no, not really. I mean, other than that one stretch I told you about... the rest of the time, I just can't shake it. I really wish I could say yes, because I want to be doing better, I really do. 

But honestly, that's the whole reason I finally made the appointment to come in. I just... I can't stop feeling like every little thing that goes wrong is completely my fault. Like, I'll just sit there thinking I'm a terrible employee, and a horrible homeowner, and that I just deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm repeating myself and I really don't want to waste your time or sound like I'm not trying to get better. It's just... that guilt is always there, telling me I don't deserve any of the good things. I hope it's okay that I'm being this honest with you... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Are there any times when you feel completely worthy of the good things in your life without any doubts or guilt that last for more than a few days?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I really wish I could give you a different answer, because I want to be the kind of person who appreciates what they have. I really try to be! 

But... no, it doesn't usually last more than a few days, if that. That's... that's why I'm here, honestly. I just, um... I have this constant feeling that everything bad that happens is entirely my fault. I just sit there and think about how I'm such a bad employee, and a terrible homeowner, and... and that I just deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for. 

I'm so sorry, I know I'm basically a broken record at this point. I really don't want to frustrate you or make you think I'm not trying to be positive. I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly. Is... is this the kind of information you need? I really hope I'm being helpful.
Do you ever have a whole week where you don't feel worthless at all?

Um... no, not a whole week. I really, really wish I could say yes. I know I keep saying the same thing, and I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you the progress you want to hear about. 

But honestly, that feeling of worthlessness... that's the main reason I finally made myself come in. I just... I can't stop this feeling that every single thing that goes wrong is entirely my fault. I'll just be sitting there, thinking about how I'm a bad employee, and a bad homeowner, and that I just... I deserve to lose everything I've worked for. 

I'm trying so hard to be better, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in it. I just... I can't seem to shake it for a whole week. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay... I really just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on.
Have you felt worthless for most of the past two years?

Um... yeah, I guess it has been. Looking back at it all... the low mood and just... losing interest in everything... it's been there for almost the entire time since this all started. 

I mean, there have been some brief periods where I could function a little better, and I really try to make the most of those days! I promise I do. I always hope that means I'm finally getting back to normal. But mostly, the low feeling just kind of stays. 

I'm so sorry, I know it probably sounds like I'm just not trying hard enough to get over it, or like I'm not doing my part. I really hope it's okay that I'm telling you this... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact information you need to figure this out. Did I answer that okay?
Are there any times when you feel completely worthy of the good things in your life for an extended period, such as several months?

Um... no, not for several months. I mean, I really wish I could say yes, because I know I'm probably starting to sound like a broken record, and I'm so sorry about that. I really don't want to seem like I'm not trying to get better. 

But looking back at it all... the low mood and just losing interest in everything... it's honestly been there for almost the whole time since this all started. There have been some brief periods where I could function a little better, and I really, really try to hold onto those moments when they happen! I promise I do. I always try to use those days to catch up on everything at work and around the house. 

But yeah, it hasn't lasted for months at a time. I hope it's okay that I'm just being totally honest about it. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can help me. Is that... is that the kind of detail you were looking for?
